name: Stripe
summary: A recruiter screen, a skills assessment and team interviews, with practical engineering problems drawn from payments-style work.

process.note: Stripe outlines the general shape of its process and says timelines vary by role. Round contents are what candidates commonly report.

stages.name: Recruiter screen
stages.detail: Most processes start with a conversation with a recruiter about the role and your background.

stages.name: Skills assessment
stages.detail: A technical or skills assessment comes next; for engineers this is commonly a practical coding exercise.

stages.name: Team interviews
stages.detail: A series of interviews with the team. Candidates often describe practical coding, debugging and design rounds.

stages.name: Decision
stages.detail: Stripe says it aims to give clear feedback at each stage of the process.

design.note: Design rounds are commonly reported for experienced roles, often around reliable money movement and public APIs.

values.title: Stripe's operating principles
values.summary: Stripe publishes operating principles alongside its mission to grow the GDP of the internet. The names are Stripe's; the readings are ours.

items.name: Users first
items.gist: Start from what users need and treat their trust as a serious responsibility.

items.name: Create with craft and beauty
items.gist: Care about the quality of the details, because they show care for the user.

items.name: Move with urgency and focus
items.gist: Go fast on what matters most and invest in what makes you faster later.

items.name: Collaborate egolessly
items.gist: Act as one team, share information, debate openly and drop weaker ideas.

items.name: Stay curious
items.gist: Keep learning how businesses and the world work, and enjoy the unfamiliar.

items.name: Obsess over talent
items.gist: Help raise the bar for who joins and help colleagues do their best work.

prompts.text: Describe a time you went out of your way to protect a user or customer who depended on your work.
Tell a story about a detail you polished that others might have skipped. Why did it matter?
Talk about a time you had to choose what not to do so an urgent goal could ship.
Share a time you let go of your own idea because a colleague had a better one.

mock.note: Follows the team interviews as commonly reported: two practical coding rounds, a design round and a conversation about how you work.
